title: Statistics
description: Build intuition for descriptive statistics, probability, sampling, estimation, hypothesis tests, and responsible interpretation.

paths.title: Descriptive Statistics
paths.description: Summarize centers, spreads, distributions, and unusual values.

paths.title: Probability and Sampling
paths.description: Understand random events, samples, bias, and sampling distributions.

paths.title: Statistical Inference
paths.description: Interpret confidence intervals, tests, effect sizes, and uncertainty.

cards.title: Statistics turns variation into evidence
cards.prompt: Statistics provides tools for describing variability and drawing cautious conclusions from incomplete data.
cards.content: Every dataset varies. Statistical reasoning asks whether a pattern is large, stable, and relevant enough to support a decision.

cards.title: The mean is sensitive to extreme values
cards.prompt: The arithmetic mean uses every value, so one extreme observation can move it substantially.
cards.content: The median is often more representative for skewed distributions, but the best summary depends on the question and data-generating process.

cards.title: Choose a robust center
cards.prompt: Household incomes are strongly right-skewed. Which center is usually more representative of a typical household?

question.explanation: The median is less affected by a small number of very high incomes.

cards.title: Compute descriptive statistics
cards.prompt: Python can calculate common summaries, but the analyst must still inspect the distribution.
cards.content: Averages should be paired with spread and sample size; a single summary cannot reveal multimodality or outliers.

code.snippet:
import numpy as np

values = np.array([12, 15, 15, 18, 40])
print(values.mean())
print(np.median(values))
print(values.std(ddof=1))
print(np.quantile(values, [0.25, 0.75]))

cards.title: Probability models uncertainty
cards.prompt: Probability assigns numerical structure to uncertain outcomes under stated assumptions.
cards.content: A probability is meaningful only with a clearly defined event and model. Real-world frequencies may differ when assumptions fail.

cards.title: Recognize independent events
cards.prompt: Two fair coin flips are performed. Does the first result change the probability of heads on the second flip?

question.explanation: For independent fair flips, the second result is unaffected by the first.

cards.title: A sample should represent its target population
cards.prompt: Sampling bias occurs when some members of the target population have systematically different chances of inclusion.
cards.content: A very large biased sample can produce a precise estimate of the wrong population quantity.

cards.title: Evaluate a sample
cards.prompt: Before generalizing, inspect how observations entered the dataset.
cards.content: Random selection helps, but nonresponse, coverage gaps, clustering, and convenience recruitment can still distort results.
items: Account for clustering or survey weights.

cards.title: Confidence intervals describe estimation uncertainty
cards.prompt: A confidence interval gives a range produced by a method that captures the true parameter at a stated long-run rate.
cards.content: It does not mean a fixed parameter has a changing probability after the interval is calculated. Interpret the method and assumptions carefully.

cards.title: A p-value is not the probability the null is true
cards.prompt: A p-value measures how incompatible the observed data are with a specified null model.
cards.content: It does not measure effect importance, practical value, or the probability that a result will replicate.

cards.title: Separate significance from importance
cards.prompt: A huge sample finds a difference of 0.01 units with p < 0.001. What else is essential?

options: A smaller font in the report
question.explanation: Statistical significance can occur for trivial effects when the sample is very large.

cards.title: Report an inferential result
cards.prompt: A complete result communicates magnitude, uncertainty, assumptions, and context.
cards.content: Avoid binary language such as proved or no effect. Evidence exists on a continuum and depends on model quality.
items: Avoid causal claims without a causal design.
